record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: Is the entanglement entropy of all quantum fields in nature, computed with causal set discreteness as a covariant ultraviolet cutoff and spacetime-correlator methods such as the Sorkin-Johnston vacuum, the complete microscopic explanation of horizon entropy or only one important contribution?

evidence.quote: In causal set theory, the entanglement entropy is expressed as a sum over solutions to a generalized eigenvalue problem involving the two-point correlation function of the theory, W(x, x′). The discreteness scale furnishes the covariant UV cutoff that makes this entropy finite.
Together with the SJ vacuum state, the application of this (entanglement) entropy definition in causal set theory in particular allows for the use of a fundamentally covariant UV cutoff.
Whether or not the entanglement entropy of all fields in nature turns out to be the full story of horizon entropy remains to be seen. It is, however, at the very least an important part of the story.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a free scalar quantum field on a globally hyperbolic spacetime (or a causal set approximating one), with two-point Wightman function W(x,x'). Define the entanglement entropy associated with a spacetime subregion R by Sorkin's spacetime formula

  S = Σ_λ λ ln|λ|,

where λ runs over the eigenvalues of the generalized eigenvalue problem

  i Δ|_R v = λ W|_R v,    with W v = λ (W − i Δ) v,

restricted to R, and Δ(x,x') = W(x,x') − W(x',x) is the Pauli–Jordan commutator. In the causal set setting, take W to be the Sorkin–Johnston (SJ) vacuum two-point function, defined as the positive part of the spectral decomposition of i Δ on the causal set, so that the fundamental discreteness scale provides a covariant ultraviolet cutoff rendering S finite.

For a causal horizon (e.g. a Rindler or black-hole horizon) in the continuum limit, let S_ent denote the sum over all quantum fields in nature of the entanglement entropy defined above associated with the exterior of the horizon, and let S_hor denote the Bekenstein–Hawking horizon entropy A/(4 G ℏ) (including any required higher-curvature corrections).

Question: Is S_ent equal to S_hor (so that entanglement entropy computed with causal set discreteness as the covariant UV cutoff, together with the Sorkin–Johnston vacuum, provides the complete microscopic explanation of horizon entropy), or does S_ent account only for a proper, non-trivial part of S_hor with additional contributions required?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether quantum field entanglement entropy across a horizon fully accounts for the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, or only contributes to it, remains an open conceptual problem in quantum gravity. While causal set computations using the SJ vacuum yield finite area-law entropies, the conjectured exact identification with horizon entropy for all fields in nature has not been established and is still under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Entanglement entropy in causal set theory
status_evidence.snippet: Sorkin-Johnston vacuum entanglement entropy in causal sets yields a finite, covariant area law in 2D and 4D, supporting the entropy-area connection but not establishing full horizon entropy completeness.
status_evidence.claim: Causal set EE matches horizon area law but completeness as full microscopic explanation is unresolved.
